seoTitle: How to Fully Remove a Google Workspace Account 2026
metaDescription: Shutting down Google Workspace? Here's how to sign in as admin, remove users, cancel billing, delete the organization, and release your domain safely.
intro: Closing out a Google Workspace account involves more than canceling a subscription — you need to sign into the Admin Console as an administrator, work through the Account section to reach organization deletion, remove users, cancel billing, and decide what happens to your domain. This guide follows the real Admin Console screens for that process, from picking the right administrator account at sign-in to finding the Account settings where deletion actually lives. It's aimed at freelancers, startups, and small business owners who signed up for a trial or a short-term project and now want to shut things down cleanly, without getting billed again or losing data they meant to keep.

steps.heading: Sign in with your administrator account
steps.body: Head to admin.google.com and Google will prompt you to choose which account to continue with — this matters because only an account with administrator privileges can reach the settings needed to remove the organization. If you manage several Workspace accounts, as many freelancers and agencies do, take a second to confirm you're picking the right one before continuing; the account picker lists the email address under each profile name so you can check the domain matches the Workspace you're actually closing.

image.caption: Google's account picker at admin.google.com. Deleting a Workspace organization requires signing in with an administrator account, not a regular user login.

steps.heading: Back up anything you need before deleting
steps.body: Before touching removal settings, download any emails, Drive files, or other data tied to the organization that you want to keep, since deleting a Workspace account removes access to that content for good. Google Takeout, reachable from your account settings, lets you export Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and other services in bulk rather than pulling files one at a time. This step is easy to skip when you're in a hurry to stop being charged, but it's the one you can't undo after the fact.

steps.heading: Search the Admin Console if you're not sure where to start
steps.body: The Admin Console's search bar at the top of the screen accepts plain-language queries, and typing something like "remove" pulls up related help articles alongside matching settings. It's a useful sanity check before an irreversible action like deleting an organization — you can confirm what the deletion actually does to users, billing, and your domain before clicking anything. The settings you actually need for deletion itself live under the Account section of the left-hand menu, not under Billing or Users directly.

image.caption: Typing "REMOVE" into the Admin Console search bar surfaces related help articles — a quick way to confirm you're heading toward the right setting before you commit to deleting anything.

steps.heading: Remove users from the organization
steps.body: Under Directory in the left menu, go through the list of users and either suspend or delete each account no longer in use. Removing users individually first, rather than relying solely on organization-level deletion, gives you a chance to confirm nothing important is tied to a specific mailbox before it's gone. For a small team this only takes a few minutes; for a larger org, exporting the user list first makes it easier to track who's been handled.

steps.heading: Open the Account section to find deletion settings
steps.body: Scroll the Admin Console's left navigation past Reporting and Billing to the Account section — this is easy to miss on a first pass, since the instinct is to look for account deletion somewhere inside Billing instead. Account expands into sub-items including Account settings, where Google surfaces the option to delete the Google Workspace subscription and organization entirely. Opening it here, rather than hunting through billing menus, is the direct path to the deletion flow.

image.caption: The Admin Console's left-hand menu, scrolled down to Account — this is where organization-level settings, including deletion, live rather than under Billing.

steps.heading: Cancel billing before you delete the organization
steps.body: From the Billing section, cancel your active subscription so you're not charged again, ideally before you finalize the organization deletion — cancellation and deletion are handled as separate steps in the Admin Console. If you're mid-trial rather than a paid subscriber, this step is usually quicker since there's no active payment method to unwind, but it's still worth confirming there isn't a scheduled charge pending.

steps.heading: Release your domain if you plan to reuse it
steps.body: If the domain tied to this Workspace account should keep working with a different provider or a personal Gmail setup, release it as the final step so it isn't stuck pointing at a deleted organization. Google walks you through domain release from within the same account deletion flow, and it's worth doing in the same session rather than coming back to it later, since a domain still attached to a deleted org can complicate re-verifying ownership elsewhere.

faq.question: Will I lose my data if I delete my Google Workspace account?
faq.answer: Yes, deleting the account can permanently remove associated data, which is why it's worth downloading anything important through Google Takeout before starting the removal process.

faq.question: Do I need to cancel billing separately from deleting the account?
faq.answer: Yes — canceling billing and deleting the Workspace organization are separate steps in the Admin Console, and skipping billing cancellation risks being charged again.

faq.question: Can I keep using my domain after removing Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Yes, releasing your domain from Workspace as part of the deletion flow lets you continue using it with another email provider or purpose once the account is shut down.

faq.question: Where in the Admin Console is account deletion actually located?
faq.answer: It's under the Account section of the left-hand menu, in Account settings — not inside Billing, which is where most people first look for it.
